title: Wholesale check
intro: A sanity check on the wholesale layer in the flow model: do the biggest wholesalers in each country sell roughly what the layer says? The dashboard layer in the table is live from the flow model. The company figures come from a separate research run in October 2026, and we re-opened a selection of the sources ourselves.
findings: No country shows a wholesale layer that looks too high. For Hungary, Germany, the UK, Spain and Italy the biggest named wholesalers plausibly carry 40–95% of the layer, which is what a concentrated trade should show.
Hungary has the closest independent match: a bond document puts passenger-tyre wholesale at about 70% of the market, against 73% in the dashboard.
France, Austria, Switzerland, Belgium, Denmark and Poland cannot be tested yet, because the named wholesalers publish too little. The gaps are listed below.
The Netherlands cannot be tested from company data, and may be pointing at understated import and re-export flows. That is a question for the model, not a finding.
Nothing in the model was changed by this check. It adds evidence, caveats and corrections only.

corrections.t: Netherlands: a mistake in the research brief
corrections.x: The brief given to the research run described the Dutch wholesale layer as including re-exports. It does not: the dashboard's 6.42M is domestic, after taking off the 2.41M that Dutch wholesalers send abroad. The report's verdict that the NL figure was “far off, too low” rests on that wrong description and is withdrawn. What company data can say about the Netherlands is shown in its own block.
Bond International is an independent family company; only Micheldever is owned by a manufacturer (Sumitomo, since 2017). The earlier note calling both “independent” is corrected on the card.

The research run reported 16.8 million tyres handled and one tyre every 3.5 seconds. The two Bond pages we opened say one tyre every six seconds and give 2024 turnover of £417M. The new estimate is 5–8M, and the 16.8M is not used.

Distri Cash 6.0M against 6.5M (and 5.5M in 2022); NEX 2.5M and €200M+ against 3.6M and €290.4M; Göggel €490M against €256M; Best4Tires about €600M against €508M; Bond 11 distribution centres against five.

method: The test: add up what the biggest wholesalers say they sell and compare it with the wholesale layer in the flow model. If they alone exceeded the layer, the layer would be too low. If they covered a tiny share of a layer that should be concentrated, it might be too high.

It is a sanity check, not a measurement. Company figures cover all tyre types (cars, trucks, motorbikes, agricultural), include exports and some own retail, and use different years. So they are ceilings for domestic passenger-car wholesale, not exact matches.
Where only revenue is known, tyres are derived at €60–100 a tyre. That range is wide on purpose.

countries.headline: The five biggest names plausibly carry about 60% of the 24.7M wholesale layer. Nothing points to the layer being too high.
countries.sumNote: Research run's range for the named group's domestic car tyres. The company figures below are larger because they include trucks, exports and own retail.

named.name: Reifen Göggel
named.label: DERIVED
named.src: Reifenpresse, via Schwäbische Zeitung (research run); same figure on the card from Neue Reifenzeitung 8/2024
named.caveat: DDW shows €256M instead, which would give 2.6–4.3M tyres. Not resolved.

named.name: Best4Tires
named.label: CLAIM
named.basis: Nearly 6 million tyres; the research run puts revenue near €600M, the card has €508M for the group.
named.caveat: Revenue €600M (research run) against €508M group revenue (Neue Reifenzeitung 8/2024, on the card).

named.name: Pneuhage / Interpneu
named.label: DERIVED
named.basis: €543M wholesale revenue ÷ €100 to €60. Includes truck tyres, so the car-tyre part is lower.
named.src: Neue Reifenzeitung 8/2024 (card); group figure from Reifenpresse (research run)

named.name: Reifen Müller (Hankook)
named.label: DERIVED
named.basis: €282M ÷ €100 to €60. Includes retail, so the wholesale part is lower.

evidence.x: BRV puts car-tyre sales at “knapp 41 Millionen Stück” (just under 41 million), which matches the dashboard's 41.0M. It also adds about 4.1M van tyres (kfz-betrieb), which the Germany flow does not include because it is still car-and-4x4 only.
Roland Berger (Nov 2018): around 50 tyre wholesalers in Germany, the top 7 holding about 75%. Five names at about 60% fits that.

gaps: The 2024 wholesaler ranking in Neue Reifenzeitung is behind a paywall, so the 2024 revenues are not confirmed.
Reifen Helm, Burkhardt and Ihle publish no tyre volumes.

countries.headline: One name, Distri Cash, already covers about 35–42% of the 15.5M layer. That is enough to show the layer is not too high, but too little to test it.
countries.sumNote: Distri Cash only. The other eight names on the card publish no tyre volumes.

named.label: PUBLISHED
named.basis: Printed in J2R, 15 Jul 2023: 700,000 more than in 2021.
named.quote: Historiquement dans la distribution de pneumatiques, Distri Cash en a écoulé plus de 5,5 millions sur l’année.
named.en: Historically in tyre distribution, Distri Cash sold more than 5.5 million over the year.

named.fig: 6.5M tyres and €573M; or 6M and €625M including €90M of parts
named.label: CLAIM
named.basis: Two versions of the same company, both from the research run.
named.caveat: The two versions differ (6.0M against 6.5M). An older Auto Infos item said 3.5M tyres, about 10% share.

evidence.x: The older Auto Infos item (3.5M tyres = about 10% share) implies a market near 35M, which fits the dashboard's 37.1M.

gaps: AAG, Doyen/Autodis, Copadex, Chrono, DPI, Massa, Alzura and Exadis: no tyre volumes found.
No concentration statistic for French tyre wholesale was found.

countries.headline: Micheldever and Bond together handle roughly 11.5–14.5M tyres, about 55–70% of the 21.0M layer. Part of that layer is manufacturer-owned.
countries.sumNote: Micheldever 6.5M plus Bond 5–8M, our own re-check. The research run had 10–15M.

named.name: Micheldever Tyre Services
named.unit: tyres a year handled, all types
named.label: PUBLISHED
named.basis: Of this, its own 184 Protyre centres fit 1.35M a year, so about 5.2M goes to other trade customers.
named.src: Fleet News, feature on Micheldever (iQ issue, Jun 2026)
named.quote: handling 6.5 million tyres a year from budget to premium lines.
named.caveat: The research run quoted “around six million tyres each year to more than 6,000 retailers” (older company wording). The 6.5M above is newer.

named.name: Bond International
named.label: DERIVED
named.basis: One tyre every six seconds is 5.3M a year if counted around the clock. £417M, taken as about €490M, ÷ €100 to €60 gives 4.9–8.2M. Both point to about 5–8M.
named.src: Supply Chain World, 28 Aug 2025 (turnover) and Bond's own website via the Tyrepress directory (the six-second rate)
named.quote: In 2018, our turnover was £162 million, but in 2024, this figure grew to £417 million
named.caveat: The research run reported “16.8 million tyres last year” and “one tyre every 3.5 seconds”. Neither wording appears on the two pages we opened, which say every six seconds. Treated as not supported. The website also says 11 distribution centres, while the August 2025 interview says five.

evidence.x: Bond is independent and family-owned: “We are proud to have remained an independent family company for over 59 years.” Only Micheldever is manufacturer-owned (Sumitomo, which owns Dunlop). An earlier note on the card called Micheldever independent; that is corrected.
Micheldever: 1,600 independent partners, 80% of that business with 250 “tier one” operators (Fleet News).

gaps: Stapleton's and Group Tyre: no volumes found. Companies House accounts for Bond are the next best source.

countries.headline: Company data cannot test the 6.42M domestic figure. It does hint that Dutch wholesalers move more tyres across the border than the model's 2.84M in and 2.41M out.

named.name: Inter-Sprint (Global Automotive Investments)
named.unit: tyres a year, all types, all countries
named.label: DERIVED
named.basis: €947M ÷ €100 to €60. This is the whole group, not the Dutch market, and includes truck and other types, so the true passenger-car count is lower.
named.caveat: The card also carries an EW Top 500 revenue of €1.93bn for the whole holding (not checked).

named.name: Inter-Sprint warehouse
named.fig: About 2.8 million tyres in 200,000 m² of warehouse
named.label: PUBLISHED
named.basis: A stock figure, not a yearly volume.
named.quote: housing around 2.8 million tyres in 200,000 square metres of warehousing

evidence.x: The 6.42M is domestic: tyres Dutch wholesalers sell in the Netherlands, after taking off the 2.41M they send abroad. Company revenue is mostly export, so it cannot confirm or reject the domestic figure.

evidence.t: What the data may be saying
evidence.x: One group's revenue implies a throughput above the model's 6.42M domestic plus 2.41M export (about 8.8M). The scopes differ, so this is a prompt to look at the import and re-export boxes, not a finding.

gaps: Dutch wholesale volumes by company are not published. Annual accounts of Inter-Sprint and Van den Ban are the next best source.

countries.headline: Deldo is mostly an export business, so it says little about the Belgian layer. The flow has no wholesale figure yet; the research run's indication is shown for reference only.
